tasks.short: Review prescription accuracy, ingredients and suitability

steps.what: Verify prescriptions against patient identity, medicines and relevant clinical information
Review ingredient, dose, interaction and contraindication references for prescriptions
Evaluate suitability and resolve prescription discrepancies with the prescriber

tasks.design: Configure the pharmacy record {OTHER} to show prescription fields beside current medication rules and source details. The pharmacist verifies inputs, interprets alerts and resolves discrepancies; dispensing and prescription changes remain outside this review boundary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant reference details may require repeated navigation even when surveillance already runs.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views can reduce navigation around existing deterministic surveillance.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete histories, alert relevance and clinical suitability for an individual patient.
tasks.human_edge: The pharmacist can question an apparently valid prescription and resolve uncertainty with the prescriber.
tasks.altitude: Less reference navigation; the clinical review remains accountable professional work.

reach.task: Identify missing prescription fields for pharmacist review
reach.learn: Data verification and escalation without clinical substitution

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates with content set by KNMP; this is existing surveillance capability, not evidence of new labour savings.
A consolidated native view may reduce reference navigation while clinical review stays manual; allocations are modelled.

assumptions: Boundary is prescription review, excluding dispensing, prescribing and medication counselling. No gain is attributed to already automated surveillance.

Prescriber produces prescription patient identifier, drug, strength, form, dose, route, frequency and quantity through the existing prescribing workflow. Its unchanged capture is outside pharmacist time. Pharmacist verifies and captures missing medication, allergy and clinical context in s1, with its full 35 hours retained.

s2 retains 24 hours for source checking, navigation exceptions and alert interpretation. Unknown clinical fields block definitive assessment and require manual clarification in s3; no absence of allergy is inferred.
Test native configuration first. Local scope determines what the pharmacist may change; this design grants no prescribing authority.
unknowns: Current surveillance and screen navigation burden
Completeness and access to clinical context
research_questions: Does a consolidated reference view reduce review time without reducing detection of clinically meaningful discrepancies?

incremental.description: Check field mappings, reference versions and display omissions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=35+24+35=94; gross 6 minus 2 upkeep gives net 4. High requires fragmented reference navigation; low removes only 2 hours, consumed by upkeep. Existing rule execution and clinical decision time yield no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate on drug-regimen quality and effectiveness

steps.what: Gather drug regimen evidence and reference information for collaborative review
Evaluate drug quality, effectiveness and applications in the patient's context
Collaborate with health care professionals and provide advice on drugs

tasks.design: Configure source bookmarks and a review view across the pharmacy record {OTHER} and approved references in {DOCS}. The pharmacist checks evidence, evaluates regimen effectiveness and discusses recommendations with clinicians; no treatment order is issued automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly finding current results and reference passages fragments preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native search and linked source views can shorten retrieval.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting outcomes, competing risks and patient goals with other professionals.
tasks.human_edge: The pharmacist can explain trade-offs and challenge a regimen that meets simple rules but does not work for the patient.
tasks.altitude: A little less preparation search; collaborative judgement keeps its time.

reach.task: Clarify observations needed to evaluate a regimen

evidence.claim: Linked source views can shorten preparation retrieval without replacing regimen evaluation or professional discussion; savings are a modelled scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is pharmacist preparation and collaboration, not another professional's time, repeat prescription review or order execution.

Pharmacist selects patient, regimen, clinical question, result date and source version in retained s1 time of 20 hours. Nurses and laboratory staff produce observations and results through unchanged existing work; their capture earns no pharmacist saving.
No complete structured outcomes feed is assumed; missing or conflicting results require manual checking in retained s1 and s2.
Try native views before custom integration. Existing navigation shortcuts earn no new gain. Regimen evaluation and professional contact remain unchanged.
unknowns: Actual retrieval burden and result access
research_questions: Can a linked source view shorten preparation without overlooking contradictory monitoring evidence?

incremental.description: Maintain source links and check result displays

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=20+30+45=95; gross 5 minus 2 upkeep gives net 3. High assumes fragmented retrieval; low removes only 2 hours, offset by upkeep. No reduction is assigned to discussion or assessment.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide specialist pharmacy service in hospitals and clinics

steps.what: Assess specialist drug therapy needs within hospital or clinic practice
Provide specialist consultation or dispense prescriptions within the authorised service

tasks.design: Retain specialist assessment and service delivery using the pharmacy record {OTHER}. This broad occupational description does not identify a separate repeated administrative step; specific review and reference improvements belong to their narrower tasks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specialist pharmacy service depends on clinical context, local authorisation and physical or interpersonal delivery.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference and documentation capabilities do not establish an end-to-end replacement for specialist service.
tasks.still_hard: Rare therapy risks, clinical uncertainty and safe service execution.
tasks.human_edge: The pharmacist integrates specialist experience and can stop unsafe service delivery.
tasks.altitude: No change in specialist service time or authority.

reach.task: Discuss a specialist drug-therapy concern through existing consultation

evidence.claim: A broad specialist-service description alone provides no basis for a quantified administrative saving; narrower tasks must establish it.

assumptions: Boundary is specialist assessment and service delivery; hospital, clinic and specialist therapy variants are alternatives, not an invented single universal dispensing process.
Clinical teams produce prescriptions and findings through existing authorised workflows. The pharmacist assesses these in s1; no structured suitability conclusion is assumed.
Local professional scope controls dispensing and consultation; an overseas occupational task does not grant prescribing rights.

Check native systems before any later custom proposal. This design introduces no software or process, so upkeep is zero. Overlap with prescription review and collaboration must be allocated once in a role roll-up.
unknowns: Specialty, service mix and local professional scope
research_questions: Which specific specialist-service step has removable effort beyond existing systems and the separately described review tasks?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0 give zero saving for routine and complex specialist service. No documentation baseline is invented and no narrower task's gain is counted again.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain interactions, side effects, dosage and medication storage

steps.what: Clarify the person's medication information needs and relevant clinical context
Locate and check information on interactions, effects, dosage and storage
Provide medication advice and check understanding of dosage and storage

tasks.design: Configure direct links from the pharmacy record {OTHER} to current approved medication passages in {DOCS}. The pharmacist checks applicability and explains interactions, side effects, dose and storage in the person's context, retaining understanding checks and escalation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the precise current reference passage can interrupt counselling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference links and search filters can reduce lookup without generating personal medical advice.
tasks.still_hard: Identifying what the person has misunderstood and balancing risks in context.
tasks.human_edge: The pharmacist can detect a dangerous misunderstanding and explain or escalate it immediately.
tasks.altitude: Less source hunting; patient counselling keeps its time.

reach.task: Locate the approved storage passage for pharmacist checking
reach.learn: Source currency and when questions require the pharmacist

evidence.claim: Native links to approved references may reduce lookup while personal counselling remains; the time estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is medication information and counselling, excluding prescription suitability review and dispensing.

Pharmacist clarifies the question and context in s1, then selects drug, strength, form, topic, source version and relevant passage within s2's 17.5 retained hours. No ready coded patient question or inferred medication is assumed.
Missing or conflicting sources require manual checking. Personalised advice, explanation and understanding checks stay with the pharmacist.
Test native reference links before custom software; existing links earn no new saving. No patient-facing chatbot is introduced.
unknowns: Current lookup effort and approved references
research_questions: Can direct source links reduce lookup without shortening understanding checks or increasing advice errors?

already_counted.description: Source selection, field capture and applicability check

incremental.description: Maintain source links and check changed medication information

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=20+17.5+55=92.5; gross 7.5 minus 2 upkeep gives net 5.5. High assumes repeated passage hunting; low removes 2 hours, consumed by upkeep. Clinical discussion and understanding checks retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce reference navigation while retaining prescription judgement, specialist service and patient counselling.
reach: Help technicians recognise missing fields and clinicians frame medication monitoring questions
role.ambitious_version: A pharmacist who can find current evidence promptly and explain safe medication use while keeping clinical review explicit.
